observation.visible_scene: An outdoor pile of dry brush, branches and assorted debris (including a flat board-like object at the right and a diagonal stick protruding from the left-center) burns in a grassy field. Behind it stands a line of leafless trees and shrubs under a grey, overcast sky. The camera viewpoint is fixed: the horizon, trees and the pile keep the same position in every frame.
visible_changes: The fire is already burning at the first frame and is still burning at the last; no ignition or extinguishing is shown.

Flames across the pile continuously flicker, rise, collapse and shift shape and height from frame to frame (e.g. a tall flame column on the right-center at t=0.00 wanes, then a new taller column appears near the center at t=0.20, t=0.60, t=1.00, t=1.40, etc.).
A plume of pale smoke rises from the left side of the pile and drifts upward and toward the left, its density and extent varying over time.
Glowing embers are visible within the lower part of the pile throughout, with small bright spots appearing and dimming.

The diagonal protruding stick, the flat board at the right, and the overall outline of the pile remain in essentially the same positions; the changes are in the flames and smoke, not in the bulk objects.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the fire was started, and how or when it ends, are not in this segment.
The exact composition of the burned material and whether the pile is being added to or collapsing further are not shown.
uncertain_details: The cause of the smoke's leftward drift (wind vs. convection) cannot be confirmed.
Whether any small flame licks represent separate burning pieces or just the same fuel flickering is not determinable.
Camera motion is judged absent based on stable background, but very slight drift cannot be fully excluded.
